assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of the cell is a physical-chemical idea of unusual generality: P granules and nucleoli behave as condensed liquid phases governed by concentration, valency and interaction strength. It gives a quantitative, thermodynamic framework for compartmentalisation without membranes and has opened very large fields in cell biology, disease and polymer physics of disordered proteins.
assessment.attribution: The 2009 P-granule liquid-droplet demonstration (Brangwynne, Hyman and colleagues) is the identifiable original discovery; Rosen, Pappu and Mittag supplied the multivalent-interaction and sequence-grammar framework. A two-person prize for Hyman and Brangwynne is cleanest, though omitting Rosen is a real credit question.
assessment.maturity: More than fifteen years of independent confirmation across many labs and systems, and the concept is now textbook-level, so timing is right.
uncertainties: How much of the in-cell phenomenon is true equilibrium phase separation versus other assemblies is still debated.
Whether Rosen or Pappu should share credit; a three-person split is possible but weakens the citation.
Some reported condensate functions rely on over-expression artefacts.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminator nucleotides and single-molecule/cluster imaging made DNA sequencing cheap and massively parallel, transforming biology and medicine. This is a clear chemical invention (nucleotide chemistry, fluorophore cleavage, surface chemistry) with enormous generative impact, and the principle is easy to explain to a broad audience.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman founded the Solexa chemistry and concept; Rothberg (454 pyrosequencing), Mayer (Manteia) and Ju (terminator chemistry) are parallel contributors. The two Cambridge chemists form the most defensible core, though the credit boundary with 454 and Ju needs scrutiny.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature: Illumina chemistry has dominated sequencing for over fifteen years and is validated at population scale.
uncertainties: Competing claims from Ju, Mayer and Rothberg could force a three-person or different configuration.
The 1977 Sanger prize and 2020s overlap with PCR-adjacent recognition may be argued as a close precedent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling made aryl amines accessible by a general, mechanistically understood catalytic route and is used daily in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis. Ligand design for the oxidative addition and reductive elimination steps is a clean story of mechanism leading to capability, a strong complement to the 2010 C-C coupling prize.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently and decisively developed general catalysts in the mid-1990s and later generations; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a precursor, which complicates but does not remove a two-person attribution.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and widely adopted for three decades, with no real doubt about impact.
uncertainties: Kosugi and Migita priority could be raised.
Overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling citation may make some members regard it as incremental.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling delivery chemistry for siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines; pH-dependent charge control of encapsulation and endosomal release is a rational physical-chemistry design. Its real-world impact after 2020 is exceptional and extends beyond the 2023 Medicine prize, which recognised the RNA modification, not the carrier.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues (Hope, Madden, MacLachlan) developed the ionizable-lipid LNP formulation; Anderson and Langer developed lipidoid libraries. Credit is spread over many contributors and a clean three-person split is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Validated by approved products, though the fundamental chemistry of lipid optimisation is still evolving.
uncertainties: Allocation among Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer is unresolved.
Proximity to the 2023 Medicine prize may influence the committee's view of novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single nucleic-acid molecules through a nanopore by ionic current is a physically elegant, label-free measurement principle that became a commercial long-read sequencing technology. It is single-molecule electrical detection meeting chemistry, with strong generative potential for proteins and other polymers.
assessment.attribution: Deamer, Branton and Kasianowicz proposed and first demonstrated polynucleotide translocation; Bayley engineered protein pores and chemistry; Akeson demonstrated enzyme-controlled ratcheting that made sequencing possible. Branton's death and the many contributors make a clean three-person configuration contestable.
assessment.maturity: Established by commercial use for over a decade, though accuracy and breadth continue to evolve.
uncertainties: Branton, a key originator, is deceased; Kasianowicz priority is a credit question.
Whether the invention is more physics or engineering than chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskite absorbers produced a rapid rise in solar-cell efficiency, with unusual defect tolerance and long carrier lifetimes, and a new family of solution-processable semiconductors. The physics of this defect tolerance is of great interest, and the potential for energy applications is large.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka first reported perovskite sensitisation in 2009; Park and Grätzel's 2012 solid-state cell and Snaith's 2012 meso-superstructured cell established the field. Kanatzidis and Seok also contributed; credit is crowded and sequence of key papers is debated.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency confirmed independently, but long-term stability and commercialisation remain unproven, so recognition could be premature.
uncertainties: Operational stability and lead toxicity may limit real-world impact.
Four to six plausible laureates create a contested attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterobifunctional degraders and molecular glues induce proximity between a target and an E3 ligase and so destroy proteins, a new pharmacological modality with a clear mechanistic principle and large generative potential for undruggable targets. Several compounds are in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the PROTAC concept (2001); Crews led the small-molecule development, Ciulli the structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex work. Molecular glue discoveries (Handa, Ito) add a separate strand that may need distinct recognition.
assessment.maturity: Clinical proof of benefit is still emerging, so this may be early.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug yet; maturity is uncertain.
Whether thalidomide/IMiD mechanism (Handa, Ito) belongs in the same citation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Resolving bond-level chemical structure of individual molecules with a CO-functionalised noncontact AFM tip is a striking physical measurement that gave direct images of molecules and reaction products on surfaces. It is conceptually clean and approaches atomic resolution limits, with real value for on-surface synthesis and structure assignment.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl developed the qPlus sensor, Gross, Meyer and colleagues at IBM Zurich demonstrated the bond-resolved molecular imaging and CO tip functionalisation; Eigler and Ho are earlier STM pioneers whose recognition overlaps with the 1986 Physics prize.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced in many labs for over a decade, but impact on mainstream chemistry is narrower than for other candidates.
uncertainties: Applicability beyond ultra-high-vacuum model surfaces is limited.
Overlap with physics recognition and a narrow user community.
